title: Safe to Resume? Breaking Execution Continuity of Agent Execution via Rollback
abstract: arXiv:2608.29381v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI agents are moving toward persistent, stateful execution across various applications, accumulating execution state and external effects that are costly to reconstruct after failures. Checkpoint and rollback (C/R) are becoming essential for recovery, yet their security implications remain largely unexplored. Correct rollback does not imply secure recovery: a faithfully restored checkpoint may resume an execution whose states, assumptions, and external effects never coexisted in any valid history. In this paper, we present the first systematic security study of checkpoint and rollback in existing agent systems. By examining representative agent C/R systems, we characterize the design space of existing C/R mechanisms and develop a general execution model that captures their recovery boundaries and state dependencies. translated_title: 恢复安全吗？通过回滚破坏智能体执行的连续性
translated_abstract: AI智能体正在向跨各种应用的持久化、有状态执行方向发展，其积累的执行状态和外部影响在故障发生后重建代价高昂。检查点与回滚（C/R）正成为故障恢复的关键技术，但其安全影响在很大程度上尚未被探索。正确的回滚并不意味着安全的恢复：一个被忠实还原的检查点可能会恢复一个其状态、假设和外部影响从未在任何有效历史中同时存在的执行。在本文中，我们对现有智能体系统中的检查点与回滚机制进行了首次系统性的安全研究。通过考察代表性的智能体C/R系统，我们刻画了现有C/R机制的设计空间，并开发了一个通用的执行模型来捕捉其恢复边界和状态依赖关系。基于该模型，我们识别出五种基本的故障模式，涵盖不完整或不一致的内部状态、过时的外部……
tldr: 本文首次对智能体系统中的检查点与回滚（C/R）机制进行了系统性安全研究，揭示“正确的回滚不等于安全的恢复”这一核心问题，并通过通用执行模型识别出五种基本故障模式。
en_tdlr: This paper presents the first systematic security study of checkpoint and rollback (C/R) in agent systems, revealing that correct rollback does not imply secure recovery and identifying five fundamental failure modes through a general execution model.
